albums.blurb: Trumpeter Lee Morgan cut The Sidewinder in December 1963 at Rudy Van Gelder's studio, aged 25 and fresh off a two-year retreat from the scene, with Joe Henderson on tenor, Barry Harris on piano, Bob Cranshaw on bass and Billy Higgins on drums. The title track's long boogaloo vamp was an afterthought written in the studio, but its crossover success set the commercial template Blue Note chased for the rest of the decade, and the four originals that follow it are prime, entirely instrumental hard bop.
albums.reception: The album reached No. 25 on Billboard's pop albums chart in early 1965 and became Blue Note's best-selling record to that point, its first 4,000-copy pressing selling out within days, while the title track reached No. 81 on the Hot 100.

albums.blurb: MICHELLE are a six-piece New York collective with four vocalists who trade and stack leads over production by members Julian Kaufman and Charlie Kilgore. This second album, their first for Transgressive/Atlantic after the self-made 2018 debut HEATWAVE, was the first they wrote together in the same room rather than by file-swapping, and its fourteen short tracks move between R&B, indie pop and disco-leaning grooves.
albums.reception: Dork rated the album four stars and called it "a complete joy from start to finish", while Loud and Quiet scored it 7/10 and likened its smooth opening cuts to labelmate Arlo Parks.

albums.blurb: Orchestra Baobab were the house band of Dakar's Baobab Club in the 1970s, blending Cuban son with Wolof and Casamance songcraft, and they dissolved in the mid-1980s as Youssou N'Dour's faster mbalax took over Senegal. After the reissue of their classic Pirates Choice revived interest, the original core - guitarist Barthélémy Attisso, singers Balla Sidibé and Rudy Gomis, saxophonist Issa Cissoko - reconvened and recorded this comeback, their first album in about fifteen years, over ten days in London with producers Nick Gold and Youssou N'Dour.
albums.reception: The album was nominated for the Grammy for Best Contemporary World Music Album, and Robert Christgau graded it A-, calling the reunion an ideal introduction to the band's relaxed mastery.
